([[Federal Way, Washington]]) | college = * [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]] (2020–2021) * [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]] (2021–2022) | highlights = * [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] Sixth Man of the Year (2022) * First-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] (2022) * [[American Athletic Conference|AAC]] All-Freshman Team (2021) }} '''Tari Eason''' (born May 10, 2001) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati Bearcats]] and the [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU Tigers]]. ==High school career== Eason started his high school career at [[Garfield High School (Seattle)|Garfield High School]] in [[Seattle|Seattle, Washington]] under head coach [[Brandon Roy]], and played sparingly during his first two years.{{cite web |last1=Evans |first1=Jayda |title=Garfield’s four-star prospect Tari Eason honors aunt with commitment to Cincinnati |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/high-school/garfields-four-star-prospect-tari-eason-honors-aunt-with-commitment-to-cincinnati/ |website=[[The Seattle Times]] |access-date=November 28, 2021 |date=December 21, 2019}} For his junior season, he transferred to [[Federal Way High School]] in [[Federal Way, Washington]], where he played alongside top recruit [[Jaden McDaniels]].{{cite web |last1=Smith |first1=Lauren |title=Federal Way's Tari Eason has been to the Tacoma Dome, but hasn't played. With the Eagles, he could be the key to a 4A title |url=https://www.thenewstribune.com/sports/high-school/article226792899.html |website=[[The News Tribune]] |access-date=November 28, 2021 |date=February 28, 2019}} Eason returned to Garfield for his senior season as Roy came back following a one-year break. He led his team to a 3A state title, recording 21 points and 14 rebounds against [[Paolo Banchero]] and [[O'Dea High School]] in the final, and received tournament MVP.{{cite web |last1=Buhler |first1=Andy |title=‘We need you to be superman.’ Tari Eason takes final bow in Garfield’s dominant 3A state championship win over O’Dea |url=https://scorebooklive.com/washington/2020/03/07/we-need-you-to-be-superman-tari-eason-takes-final-bow-in-garfields-dominant-3a-state-championship-win-over-odea/ |website=SBLive |access-date=November 28, 2021 |date=March 7, 2020}}{{cite web |last1=Buhler |first1=Andy |title=Watch: Garfield’s Tari Eason reacts to winning 3A state title, tournament MVP |url=https://scorebooklive.com/washington/2020/03/08/watch-garfields-tari-eason-reacts-to-winning-3a-state-title-tournament-mvp/ |website=SBLive |access-date=November 28, 2021 |date=March 8, 2020}} Eason averaged 23 points, eight rebounds and three steals per game as a senior, and was named 3A Player of the Year.{{cite web |last1=Springer |first1=Scott |title=Highly-touted forward Tari Eason makes it official signing with UC basketball |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/university-of-cincinnati/2020/04/20/state-washington-standout-tari-eason-signs-cincinnati-basketball/5150092002/ |website=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]] |access-date=November 28, 2021 |date=April 20, 2020}}{{cite web |title=Tari Eason |url=https://lsusports.net/sports/mb/roster/player/tari-eason/ |website=LSU Athletics |access-date=November 28, 2021}} A four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], he committed to playing college basketball for [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]] over offers from [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado]] and [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]].{{cite web |last1=Evans |first1=Corey |title=Cincinnati wins out with four-star forward Tari Eason |url=https://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/news/cincinnati-wins-out-with-four-star-forward-tari-eason |website=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=November 28, 2021 |date=December 22, 2019}} ==College career== On February 26, 2021, Eason posted a freshman season-high 20 points, 13 rebounds and three blocks in a 91–71 win over [[Tulane Green Wave men's basketball|Tulane]].{{cite web |title=Davenport carries Cincinnati over Tulane 91–71 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401277854 |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=November 28, 2021 |date=February 26, 2021}} As a freshman at Cincinnati, he averaged 7.3 points, 5.9 rebounds, 1.3 blocks and 1.2 steals per game, earning [[American Athletic Conference]] All-Freshman Team honors. For his sophomore season, Eason transferred to [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]].{{cite web |last1=Jenkins |first1=Keith |title=Former Cincinnati Bearcats All-AAC freshman forward Tari Eason transfers to LSU |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/university-of-cincinnati/2021/04/20/cincinnati-bearcats-basketball-tari-eason-transfers-lsu/7298528002/ |website=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]] |access-date=November 28, 2021 |date=April 20, 2021}} He was named to the First Team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] as well as SEC Sixth Man of the Year.{{cite press release|url=https://www.secsports.com/article/33453309/men-basketball-all-sec-teams-awards-announced|title=Men's Basketball All-SEC Teams & Awards Announced |publisher=[[Southeastern Conference]] |date=March 8, 2022 |accessdate=March 8, 2022}} Eason averaged 16.9 points, 6.6 rebounds and 1.9 steals per game.{{cite news |last1=Bates |first1=Greg |title=LSU's Tari Eason on his next step: 'I have no idea what the future holds' |url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/sports/lsu/article_3ce8ae9c-a736-11ec-8ea4-6bf52f512212.html |access-date=March 19, 2022 |work=[[The Advocate (Louisiana)|The Advocate]] |date=March 18, 2022}} On March 25, 2022, he declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite news |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Tari Eason to leave LSU Tigers basketball team, declare for NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33595126/tari-eason-leave-lsu-tigers-basketball-team-declare-nba-draft?platform=amp |access-date=March 28, 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=March 25, 2022}} ==Career
